correctness.rationale: PASS: The proposed cross-distances satisfy the triangle inequalities exactly because each within-fibre diameter≤2. Adjacent independent fibre samples give (mi−mi+1)²+vi+vi+1≤1; for gap≥2, the equal-mixture range bound gives (mi−mj)²+2(vi+vj)≤(j−i)². Summation with the variance pair identity proves the stated exact nonnegative deficits and n≥4 sharp bound. Endpoint saturation forces n=4 interior fibre constants by interval intersection; n≥5 positive variance coefficients ensure full rigidity. The separate n=3 identity 9(2/3−Var)=(a+b)²+3v1+3(λ01+λ12) gives precisely the endpoint balance case; n=2 K_2,2 attains Var=1/2. Independent rational feasible profiles for n=3,4,5 confirmed the deficit, n=3 equality and n=2 boundary.

value.rationale: PASS: Whether replacing path levels by arbitrary metric fibres can increase sharp centered Lipschitz norm is a natural structural question. The result gives a sharp n=2→3 preservation cutoff and n=3→4 optimizer rigidity threshold plus exact stability deficit, nontrivial over arbitrary fibre sizes, internal distances and conditional weights. This is a mathematically useful invariant and equality classification beyond old path spread.

final_claim: For n≥3 finite nonempty metric fibres of diameter ≤2, with cross-fibre distances |i−j| and exactly 1/n mass on each fibre (strictly positive atoms), maximum 1-Lipschitz variance is (n²−1)/12. For n≥4 all maximizers are signed unit-slope functions constant on fibres; n=3 has a complete balanced endpoint-polarization equality family. An exact nonnegative deficit identity proves rigidity, and a two-fibre K_(2,2) example shows sharp failure at n=2.
limitations: All atoms must have strictly positive weight for pointwise maximizer classification.
n=3 polarized endpoint choices must remain 1-Lipschitz under their internal fibre distances; no claim that every abstract endpoint ± assignment is feasible.
